We can use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta 
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3{cos}^{2}⁡x+1-3{sin}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int [3({cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x)+1]\text{d}x \\  & =\int (3\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1)\text{d}x \\  & =3(\frac{1}{2}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+x+C \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
